title.value: Drumming the Account: Debt Recitation, Colony Fission and the Problem of Who Owes After a Count Divides on the Soot Shelf

abstract.value: Soot Shelf colonies keep their obligations as percussive recitations drummed against the shelf, and a recitation is valid only while a count can perform it entire. We recorded nineteen full accounts and two fissions, and show that when a count divides, the debt does not divide with it: both successor counts recite the whole account, and both are held to it. Creditor counts accept this arrangement and describe a fission as an improvement in their position. We could not establish what happens when a count goes quiet without dividing, and the counts we asked declined to speculate.
